title: Count Covered Buildings
statement:
The city is an `n x n` grid, and `buildings[i] = [x, y]` places a building at coordinates `[x, y]`; no two buildings share coordinates. Think of `x` as the row and `y` as the column:

- another building with the same `x` lies to the **left** when its `y` is smaller, and to the **right** when its `y` is larger;
- another building with the same `y` lies **above** when its `x` is smaller, and **below** when its `x` is larger.

A building counts as **covered** when none of those four directions is empty. Return how many buildings are covered.
notes:
## Intuition

A building at `[x, y]` only cares about the buildings in its own row (same `x`: to its left or right, depending on `y`) and in its own column (same `y`: above or below, depending on `x`). It has neighbours on both sides in its row exactly when its `y` lies strictly between the smallest and the largest `y` of that row, and likewise for its `x` in its column. So each row and each column only needs its two extremes. Comparing every pair of buildings also works, but costs O(m²) for m buildings.

## Approach

1. Keep four maps: `minY` and `maxY` give, for each row `x`, the smallest and largest `y` in it; `minX` and `maxX` give, for each column `y`, the smallest and largest `x` in it.
2. One pass over `buildings` fills them: `get` the current extreme (or the building's own value when the row or column is new) and `set` the smaller or larger one.
3. A second pass tests each building: `leftAndRight` is `minY.get(x) < y < maxY.get(x)`, and `aboveAndBelow` is `minX.get(y) < x < maxX.get(y)`.
4. Count the buildings where both hold, and return `covered`.

## Example 1, step by step

Row `x = 2` holds `y` values 2, 1 and 3, so `minY.get(2) = 1` and `maxY.get(2) = 3`; column `y = 2` holds `x` values 1, 2 and 3, so `minX.get(2) = 1` and `maxX.get(2) = 3`. Every other row and column has one building. In the second pass, `[1,2]` and `[3,2]` are alone in their rows, `[2,1]` is the minimum of row 2 and `[2,3]` its maximum, so none of them is covered. `[2,2]` has `1 < 2 < 3` in both its row and its column, so `covered = 1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m), two passes with constant-time map operations.
- Space: O(m), at most one entry per distinct row or column in each map.

## Pitfalls

- The four directions run along the building's own row and column: a building diagonally up and to the left is neither above nor to the left of it (Test 4).
- Compare strictly: a building at either end of its row or column has nothing beyond it.
- Coordinates reach 10^5, so an `n x n` grid of cells is far too big; keep only each row's and column's extremes.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `minY`, `maxY` | for each row `x`, the smallest and largest `y` in it |
| `minX`, `maxX` | for each column `y`, the smallest and largest `x` in it |
| `x`, `y` | the current building's coordinates |
| `leftAndRight` | the building has neighbours on both sides in its row |
| `aboveAndBelow` | the building has neighbours above and below in its column |
| `covered` | how many covered buildings have been found |

narration.2: For each row x, remember the smallest y in it.
narration.3: For each row x, remember the largest y as well.
narration.4: For each column y, remember the smallest x in it.
narration.5: For each column y, remember the largest x as well.
narration.6: First pass: visit every building once to record the extremes of its row and column.
narration.7: Lower the smallest y of row x if this building is further left.
narration.8: Raise the largest y of row x if this building is further right.
narration.9: Lower the smallest x of column y if this building is higher up.
narration.10: Raise the largest x of column y if this building is further down.
narration.12: No building has been confirmed as covered yet.
narration.13: Second pass: test each building against the extremes of its row and column.
narration.14: It has buildings on its left and right when its y lies strictly between the extremes of row x.
narration.15: It has buildings above and below when its x lies strictly between the extremes of column y.
narration.16: It is covered only when all four directions are occupied.
narration.20: Return the number of covered buildings.
